Naturalism holds that reality is entirely natural and is understood through the sciences, including the theoretical entities those sciences posit, while positivism holds that a claim counts as knowledge only when it rests on observation and empirical verification. In jurisprudence those labels instead mark natural law—norms of universal, objective scope—against positivism as a structured, coherent legal system that states create according to their interests. That legal contrast is the circulated formulation that names a real difference between the two views.

CONFIDENCE: 80
